## Constraint Summary
- Peak 2000 rps; 50 TB per year; 20 ms p99; 2000 USD per month; 3 engineers; single region.

## Candidates
- Postgres outbox with logical replication.
- Kafka topic per event family.
- Direct writes with an application-level retry queue.

## Comparison Table
| Axis | Outbox | Kafka | Retry queue |
|---|---|---|---|
| p99 | 20 ms | 20 ms | 20 ms |
| Monthly cost | 2000 USD | 2000 USD | 2000 USD |
| Failure | replica lag | consumer lag | lost retries |

## Recommendation
The Postgres outbox. It is valid only while 2000 rps holds; above that the outbox table grows faster than vacuum can keep up, and the recommendation should be revisited.

## Detailed Design
Producers write the business row and the event in one transaction. A relay reads the outbox and publishes, marking rows as sent in the same transaction that advances its offset.

## Risks at ten times scale
- Ten times 2000 rps makes outbox vacuum the bottleneck.
- The relay becomes a single hot table.
- Retaining 50 TB per year becomes the dominant cost.

## Constraint Summary
- 2000 rps; Redis and Go; single region.

## Candidates
- Redis cluster with per-shard TTL.
- Redis with an application-side LRU.
- Postgres advisory locks.

## Comparison Table
| Axis | Sharded Redis | App LRU | Postgres |
|---|---|---|---|
| p99 | 20 ms | 20 ms | 20 ms |
| Operational surface | shard per tenant group | single cluster | existing DB |

## Recommendation
Sharded Redis. Wrong if 2000 rps is a sustained floor rather than a peak.

## Detailed Design
Keys are sharded by tenant; TTL is per shard; failover loses at most one shard's window.

## Risks at ten times scale
- Ten times 2000 rps saturates a single shard.
- Failover loses the shard window.
- Memory grows with tenants.
